Google removes Samsung's first Android ad blocker from the Play Store

Google wants the advertising money.

End of story.

You would think that Google would create a division of their company specifically dedicated to working directly with website developers, and other ad networks to redefine the nature of advertising on webpages so that they aren't intrusive, don't do pop-ups or auto-plays, don't make sites unstable, and don't inject nefarious code onto people's computers.

The rise in adblock software has been in direct correlation to the intrusive nature of advertising. It's almost like we reverted back to the late 90s and early 00s when ads were everywhere and bad sites would would try to do pop-ups all the time--it failed because people hated it and it screwed up the browsing experience. Fast forward 15 years and it's like developers never learned a damn thing, and adblocks are the consequence of that.

Google's best bet would be to not focus on changing the consumer, but the nature of advertising. If people don't need to use ad-blocking software to stop pop-ups, auto-play material, and to keep websites from being malicious and buggy, they wouldn't. Keep the bandwidth down, the ads useful and minimalistic and non-intrusive, and the revenue will keep coming in, don't and they will cut it off entirely.
